text:
maria: Heads-up — we're finalizing rerank semantics for the v3 endpoint. Need quick alignment on score shape, quota counting, and what the console should surface.
aj: Short answer: normalized float [0..1] for ranking, but keep raw logits optional. Most infra expects a monotonic score.
sienna: +1 for normalized. If models return logits it's fine as long as the API converts and returns both normalized and raw when possible. Otherwise teams re-implement differently and we get drift.
maria: Proposed minimal schema: JSON per candidate: `{\n  \"id\": \"c1\",\n  \"score\": 0.872,            // normalized 0-1\n  \"raw_score\": 3.21,       // optional model logit\n  \"model_variant\": \"rr-v2-q4\" // optional\n}`
kevin: How do we count quota here? per-request or per-candidate? Customers asking for both models.
aj: Implementation-wise we meter at two levels: routing unit (1 per API call) + score units per candidate when model does scoring. So we can expose both: request_unit and score_units.
sienna: Suggest score_units = candidates * model_weight. Model_weight is 1.0 for base models, 0.2 for small re-rankers, etc. That lets cost reflect model complexity.
maria: That matches business asks. Also need policy for fallback routing: if premium model quota exhausted, fallback to cheaper model. Does fallback consume both quotas?
aj: It should. We bill for actual compute used. So if fallback runs, score_units reflects fallback model weight and request_unit still counts once. Need to document in API and console.
kevin: For UX, console should show: per-route avg latency, score distribution histogram (0-1), percent of fallbacks, and model_affinity heatmap. Also a toggle to view raw vs normalized scores.
console-bot: New telemetry event proposed: `rerank.evaluate` with fields: route, model_variant, candidate_count, mean_score, fallback=true/false. (will add schema PR)
sienna: Also we should include calibration metadata for each model: `calibration_offset` and `scale` so product teams can understand shifts. Add `score_confidence` (0-1) optional for detectors.
maria: API example we can publish:
```
POST /v3/rerank
{
  "query": "how to make coffee",
  "candidates": ["doc_a","doc_b","doc_c"],
  "max_candidates": 50
}
```
Response sketch:
```
{
  "results": [
    {"id":"doc_b","score":0.92,"raw_score":4.5,"model_variant":"rr-v2-q4"},
    {"id":"doc_a","score":0.85,"raw_score":3.9}
  ],
  "meta": {"candidate_count":3,"model_used":"rr-v2-q4"}
}
```
aj: Important: we need a stable tie-breaker. Recommend `score` then `raw_score` then `id` lexicographic.
kevin: Edge cases: when clients submit > max_candidates (e.g., 1000) we should reject early or force server-side truncation with warning. For quotas, huge fanout needs a different quota bucket (fanout-heavy).
maria: Action item: define two quota buckets: `rerank.request` (per-call) and `rerank.score_unit` (per-candidate weighted). Also add `fanout` policy: requests with candidate_count > 200 auto-flag as "batch" and routed to batch queue.
aj: For runtime, we'll add a server-side pre-check that returns `429` with body `{ "code": "FANOUT_LIMIT", "allowed_max": 200 }` if over the hard limit. For soft limits we return `warning` in meta and still process.
sienna: Telemetry: capture score histograms per model + per-route, and push sample of top-k inputs to console (redact PII). That helps detect calibration drift.
kevin: Rollout UX: we need canary option to route X% traffic to new reranker variant. Console should show live delta in mean_score and user-facing metrics. Also quick rollback button.
maria: Make sure canary counts against dedicated quota for the variant. We shouldn't double-bill but need clear attribution in billing UI.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for rr-v2-q4-canary at 2148765300 by @aj
aj: I'll open an RFC that includes schema, quota rules, telemetry events, and console widget mockups. Please add comments on the RFC doc: https://redwood.internal/rfc/rerank-v3
maria: Great — I'll capture the dashboard requirements. Sienna can you add the calibration fields to model onboarding? Kevin can you draft billing copy for the two-unit model?
sienna: On it. I'll add `calibration` to model metadata service.
kevin: Will draft billing blurb today.
maria: Cool. Last note: let's standardize `score` precision to 3 decimals in storage/telemetry to reduce cardinality. We can keep raw_score full precision.
aj: Agreed.
maria: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
_note: No title field included per agents.md. Thread is single continuous string with messages prefixed by sender name.
